summary.title: OWASP DevSecOps Verification Standard (DSOVS)
summary.one_liner: The OWASP DSOVS is an open source framework listing baseline DevSecOps security requirements, organized into phases and numbered controls (ORG, REQ, DES, CODE, TEST, REL, OPR) that you can use to assess any software project or organisation.
takeaways: DSOVS is an open source OWASP incubator framework that defines baseline DevSecOps requirements for any software project or organisation.
Requirements are grouped by phase: organisation (ORG), requirements (REQ), design (DES), code (CODE), test (TEST), release (REL), and operations (OPR).
Each phase has named streams, such as threat modelling under DES-002, SAST under CODE-004, and DAST under TEST-002.
The page marks which controls are complete: CODE-002 Hardcoded Secrets Detection, TEST-002 DAST, and OPR-005 Vulnerability Disclosure show a checkmark, while the rest show a construction marker.
The project is led by Jamieson Vincenti O'Reilly and Yudhi Yudhistira, and accepts contributions via pull requests and questions on GitHub.
summary.summary: The page is the OWASP project landing page for the DevSecOps Verification Standard, an incubator project described as an open source framework of baseline requirements. It lists about 50 numbered streams across seven phases, from risk assessment and training through code scanning, testing, release, and operations hardening. Status markers show three streams as complete and the rest as in progress. The page also gives project leads, contribution channels, and GitHub stats (60 stars, 8 contributors, JavaScript, classification "Other"). It does not detail the individual requirements.
